headline: Oilers place Zach Hyman on injured reserve
take:
Daily Faceoff reports the Oilers have placed Zach Hyman on injured reserve, noting he has one goal in six games for Edmonton in 2026-27 and has already missed six games to injury. Oilersnation posted that Hyman is on IR with a sore neck, as per Jason Gregor.

Our numbers say the thin production so far this season is mostly a small-sample story. Hyman's own expected goals (the quality of his chances) sit at 1.84, against one actual goal, so he is about 0.84 goals short of what his shots should have produced. At even strength, EDM has controlled 47.4% of the expected goals with him on the ice, and the team's share has run about one point better without him, which is a faint signal at best. The bigger concern is the roster around him: EDM is 8-2-2, but goalies have saved 8.6 goals fewer than expected, so the record owes plenty to scoring.

On minutes, going by how the coach has used his players, Owen Michaels (12:10 a night) is next in line for Hyman's second-line minutes, and Kasperi Kapanen, the busiest man on the second power-play unit, is the likeliest to move up to the first unit.
